title: Modeling the Influence of Ionic Strength on Mineral Solubility in Concentrated Brine Solutions
authors: Hussain Al-Sairfi; M. A. Salman; Y. Al-Foudari; M. Ahmed
pillar: Brine chemistry, scaling control and mineral recovery
keywords: ionic strength; mineral solubility; concentrated brine; calcium sulfate; magnesium hydroxide; scaling control; mineral recovery; Kuwait desalination; brine valorization
summary: This study measures how ionic strength changes the solubility of calcium sulfate and magnesium hydroxide in concentrated brines collected from Kuwait desalination facilities. It identifies non-ideal behavior that can be used to time precipitation, limit scaling and improve mineral-recovery process design.

title: Mineral Extraction from Mixed Brine Solutions
authors: M. A. Salman; M. Ahmed; Hussain Al-Sairfi; Y. Al-Foudari
pillar: Brine chemistry, scaling control and mineral recovery
keywords: mixed brine; sulfate minerals; barite; celestite; calcium sulfate; saturation index; induction time; scaling control; brine valorization; resource recovery
summary: This paper evaluates sulfate-mineral recovery when high-salinity brines are mixed with seawater. A practical model predicts saturation index, precipitation yield and induction time for barite, celestite and calcium-sulfate phases under different mixing and operating conditions.

title: Membrane Materials for Desalination
authors: Hussain Al-Sairfi; Maha Atallah; Fajer Alelaj; Yousuf Alhendal; Mansour Ahmed
journal: Desalination Frontiers – Innovations and Progress in Water Purification Technologies [Online First]
keywords: desalination membranes; thin-film composites; polyamide; graphene oxide; metal-organic frameworks; aquaporins; chlorine resistance; membrane durability; membrane sustainability
summary: This open-access chapter reviews the evolution of desalination membrane materials, from cellulose acetate and polyamide thin-film composites to graphene oxide, aquaporin-based membranes and metal-organic frameworks. It compares performance, durability, chlorine resistance, fouling behavior, scalability and sustainability.

title: Membrane distillation of saline feeds and produced water: A comparative study of an air-gap and vacuum-driven modules
authors: Hussain Al-Sairfi; M. Z. A. Koshuriyan; Mansour Ahmed
pillar: Membrane distillation for seawater and produced water
keywords: air-gap membrane distillation; vacuum membrane distillation; Arabian Gulf seawater; oilfield-produced water; hypersaline water; permeate flux; salt rejection; desalination
summary: This comparative experimental study evaluates air-gap membrane distillation and vacuum membrane distillation for saline feeds, Arabian Gulf seawater and oilfield-produced water. It examines temperature, concentration, recirculation flow, air-gap depth and vacuum-space depth as determinants of permeate flux and salt rejection.

title: Performance feasibility study of direct contact membrane distillation systems in the treatment of seawater and oilfield-produced brine: the effect of hot- and cold-channel depth
authors: Hussain Al-Sairfi; M. Z. A. Koshuriyan; Mansour Ahmed
pillar: Membrane distillation for seawater and produced water
keywords: direct contact membrane distillation; DCMD; Arabian Gulf seawater; oilfield-produced brine; channel depth; polypropylene membrane; PVDF membrane; permeate flux; salt rejection
summary: This laboratory study assesses direct-contact membrane distillation for Arabian Gulf seawater and oilfield-produced brine using polypropylene and PVDF membranes. It evaluates channel depth, temperature, flow rate and feed concentration in relation to permeate flux and salt rejection.

title: Hydrodynamic Enhancement of Direct Contact Membrane Distillation Using a Corrugated Feed Channel: A Numerical Study
authors: Fajer M. Alelaj; Mansour Ahmed; Hussain Al-Sairfi; Garudachari Bhadrachari; Shimaa Zahran; Mohamed R. Elmarghany
keywords: direct contact membrane distillation; corrugated feed channel; computational fluid dynamics; temperature polarization; permeate flux; pressure drop; rib geometry; membrane-module design
summary: This numerical study models a direct-contact membrane-distillation channel fitted with rectangular corrugations. It evaluates how rib height, breadth and pitch alter hydrodynamic mixing, temperature polarization, pressure drop and permeate flux, identifying a practical trade-off between mass-transfer enhancement and hydraulic loss.

title: Adaptive Fuzzy Energy Management of Wind-Battery Systems With Flexible Desalination Load
authors: Mustafa Fadel; Fajer M. Alelaj; Hussain Al-Sairfi; Mansour Ahmed
pillar: AI-enabled renewable energy and water-energy systems
keywords: adaptive fuzzy control; energy management system; wind energy; battery degradation; reverse osmosis desalination; flexible load; state of charge; water-energy system; AI control
summary: This study develops an adaptive fuzzy energy-management system for a wind-turbine and battery system supplying a flexible reverse-osmosis desalination load. The controller coordinates wind power, battery state of charge and water production while explicitly reducing battery cycling and degradation.

title: Quantifying the Economic Loss and Operational Implications of Air Pollution on Grid-Connected PV Systems in the Arabian Peninsula: A Machine Learning-Based Analysis
authors: Mohammed A. Bou-Rabee; Fajer M. Alelaj; Hussain Al-Sairfi
pillar: AI-enabled renewable energy and water-energy systems
keywords: photovoltaic systems; air pollution; soiling losses; machine learning; Random Forest; economic loss; predictive cleaning; operation and maintenance; Arabian Peninsula; GCC solar energy
summary: This IEEE Access study uses a validated Random Forest model and counterfactual clean-air scenarios to estimate energy and financial losses caused by air pollution and module soiling in grid-connected photovoltaic systems across the Arabian Peninsula. It also proposes a predictive cleaning schedule for operation and maintenance planning.

title: Thermocapillary Droplet Flow in Small-scale Containers: the Effect of Gravity
authors: Mohammad K. Alhamli; Yousuf Alhendal; Hussain Al-Sairfi
keywords: thermocapillary flow; Marangoni effect; droplet migration; microgravity; buoyancy; Volume of Fluid; ANSYS Fluent; two-phase flow; surface tension gradient; confined container
summary: This numerical investigation tracks an FC-75 droplet suspended in silicone oil inside differentially heated cylindrical containers. Volume-of-Fluid simulations compare zero gravity, normal gravity and combined thermocapillary–buoyancy forcing and derive a practical criterion for the droplet size at which the two forces nearly balance.

title: Achieving single solid solution in equimolar AlCrCuFeNi via rapid solidification
authors: Ahmed Nassar; Hussain Al-Sairfi; Robert Cochrane; Mehmet Remzi Abul; Liam Teggin; Osama Al-Jenabi; Enrique Myro; Andrew Mullis
keywords: high-entropy alloy; AlCrCuFeNi; rapid solidification; drop tube; B2 phase; spinodal decomposition; solidification microstructure; microhardness; cooling rate
summary: This study uses a 6.5-m drop-tube facility to investigate the effect of cooling rate on equimolar AlCrCuFeNi high-entropy alloy. Rapid solidification suppresses phase complexity, produces a single B2 structure above approximately 10² K/s and increases microhardness as cooling rate rises.

title: Assessment of Membrane Distillation Modules for Seawater Desalination and Oilfield-Produced Water Treatment Applications
pillar: Membrane distillation for seawater and produced water
keywords: PhD thesis; membrane distillation; DCMD; AGMD; VMD; seawater desalination; oilfield-produced water; hypersaline brine; salt rejection; Kuwait
summary: This doctoral thesis experimentally evaluates direct-contact, air-gap and vacuum membrane-distillation modules for seawater, synthetic saline feeds and oilfield-produced water. It examines membrane material, temperature, salinity, flow rate and channel or gap dimensions to establish performance and design guidance under Kuwait-relevant conditions.
